In this paper, we design a MUSIC-type imaging function using scattering parameter data to find small anomaly and explore its mathematical structure. Introduction Retrieving of unknown targets from scattered field or scattering parameter data in multi-static mea- surement environment has been of great interest for many years in both inverse scattering problem and microwave imaging due to its various potential applications such as non-destructive evaluation [1, 2, 3], biomedical imaging [4, 5, 6], radar imaging [7, 8, 9]. To this ends, various reconstruction algorithms have been proposed and they are classified as iterative (or quantitative) and non-iterative (or qualitative) meth- ods. We refer to remarkable researches [10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16] for the description of various iterative and non-iterative techniques in both inverse scattering problems and microwave imaging. MUltipleSIgnalClassification(MUSIC)algorithmisawell-known,promisingqualitativemethodinboth inverse scattering problem and microwave imaging. From the pioneering research by Devaney [17], MUSIC was successfully applied for identifying point-like scatterers in multi-static measurement data. After the successful application, it has been applied various inverse scattering problems such as identification of two- and three-dimensional small targets [18, 19], fast imaging of crack-like defects [20, 21], detection of internal corrosion [22], imaging of buried targets [23, 24], limited-aperture and limited-view problems [25, 26] as well as microwave imaging such as damage assessment for intricate structures [27], through-the-wall radar imaging [28], time-reversal imaging [29], radar imaging [30], anomaly detection from scattering matrix [31], breast cancer detection [32], and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging [33]. Let us emphasize that for a successful application of MUSIC in microwave imaging, the generated scat- teringmatrixwhoseelementsarescatteringparametersmustbesymmetric. Ifthematrixisnon-symmetric, it is impossible to apply the MUSIC directly. Due to this reason, most of researches has been performed with the strong assumption that the antenna can transmit and receive signals, i.e., switching devices can be used. However, the issue of microwave imaging without a switching device may also exist as a result of limited system configurations. Instead of increasing total number of antennas, we investigate a method of arranging the antennas for obtaining a better result based on the elimination of unnecessary extra terms that disturb the detection in the imaging function. Concluding Remarks In this paper, we designed an imaging function of MUSIC for identifying small anomalies from the scattering matrix without a switching device. Based on the analyzed structure of the designed imaging function, we confirmed that the imaging performance of the MUSIC significantly depends on the total numberoftransmittersandreceivers. Additionally,theanalyzedstructurealsoallowsustofindtheoptimal antenna arrangement for obtaining better imaging results via MUSIC. To support the derived theoretical result, we presented various numerical simulation results from synthetic and experimental data. Here,weconsideredtheidentificationofsmalltargets. Extensiontotheidentificationofarbitraryshapes targets such as large anomaly, crack-like defects, etc., will be the forthcoming work. Moreover, to obtain better imaging results, development of proposed MUSIC algorithm will be an interesting topic for future research. JSON: Name: music_noswitch_antenna_optimization Title: MUSIC-type imaging for detection of small anomalies from non-symmetric scattering-parameter data without switching devices Short Hypothesis: For multi-static measurements acquired without a switching device, a MUSIC-type imaging function that explicitly uses the left- and right-singular vector structure of the non-symmetric scattering matrix and optimized transmit/receive antenna arrangements will reduce localization error and increase anomaly detection accuracy (Jaccard index) relative to (a) naive MUSIC on the non-symmetric matrix and (b) conventional MUSIC assuming a symmetric matrix, under the same number of antennas and noise conditions. Related Work: Existing microwave imaging and inverse-scattering methods split into iterative quantitative solvers and qualitative non-iterative approaches; MUSIC is a widely used qualitative method that localizes small/point-like scatterers by exploiting signal/noise subspaces derived from a symmetric multi-static scattering matrix. Prior applications of MUSIC assume reciprocity or a switching device so that the measured S-parameter matrix is symmetric/Hermitian; when measurements are non-symmetric (no switching), direct application of conventional MUSIC is invalid or produces artifacts. Limitations of current approaches include sensitivity to limited aperture and limited numbers of transmitters/receivers, strong dependence on Born approximation validity, and the need to increase antenna counts or measurement diversity to reduce artifacts. Antenna-arrangement heuristics have been suggested but lack a principled analytic link to the MUSIC imaging function for non-symmetric data and do not address the extra artifact terms arising from left/right singular vector mismatch. Abstract: This project studies detection of small electromagnetic anomalies from multi-static scattering-parameter measurements acquired without a switching device, where the measured S-matrix is non-symmetric. We propose and validate a MUSIC-type imaging function constructed from the left- and right-singular vectors associated with the nonzero singular values of the non-symmetric scattering matrix. We analytically characterize the imaging functional as a superposition of a Bessel-kernel term that yields the desired localization and additional antenna-dependent artifact terms. Building on that structure, we evaluate and identify antenna arrangements that suppress artifact contributions and improve imaging performance without increasing total antenna count. The main contribution is (i) the derivation of the imaging functional structure for non-symmetric S-parameters, and (ii) an experimental and synthetic evaluation showing when and how antenna arrangement and transmitter/receiver allocation recover localization performance comparable to symmetric (switched) setups. Expected outcomes are validated design rules for antenna placement and quantified performance bounds across SNR, frequency, and array configurations. Experiments: Datasets: (1) Synthetic dataset: CST-simulated S-parameter matrices at fixed frequencies f={0.9,1.0,1.2} GHz for a circular ROI (radius 0.08 m) with S=16 uniformly placed potential antenna sites on a ring R=0.09 m; generate 100 randomized trials per condition with single- and multi-anomaly scenarios. Anomalies: disk radii α∈{0.005,0.01,0.02} m, dielectric contrasts (ε/ε0,σ)∈{(45,1.0),(55,1.2)} as in the report. Noise: additive complex Gaussian noise to S-parameters at SNR levels {5,10,20,40} dB. (2) Experimental dataset: measured S-parameter matrices from the ETRI microwave testbed at f=925 MHz for single- and multiple metallic and dielectric inclusions; repeatable placements with 30 trials per configuration. Baselines: (A) conventional MUSIC applied assuming symmetric matrix (requires virtual symmetrization), (B) naive MUSIC applied directly to non-symmetric K, (C) matched-filter imaging using incident-field backprojection, (D) iterative Born-based inversion (single-step linearized least-squares). Evaluation metrics: localization error (Euclidean distance between estimated peak and true center), Jaccard index for detected region vs ground truth (threshold sweep and report AUC), detection rate (TPR at fixed FPR levels 1%,5%), false-positive count per image, peak-to-sidelobe ratio, and runtime per reconstruction. Experimental setup: for each trial vary transmit set B and receive set A such that M,N∈{2,4,8,12,16} with both symmetric and intentionally non-overlapping allocations; evaluate antenna-arrangement schemes: uniform interleaved (RX/TX alternating), clustered, random. Number of singular vectors: retain first r singular values where r∈{1,2,3} (ablation). Ablation studies: (i) effect of M vs N (fix total S), (ii) effect of antenna arrangement on E_RX/E_TX artifact magnitude, (iii) impact of frequency and Born approximation (compare results across f and contrast/size values), (iv) sensitivity to SNR. Statistical testing: report mean±std over trials and perform paired significance testing (Wilcoxon signed-rank) between proposed method and each baseline for localization error and Jaccard AUC. Risk Factors and Limitations: Breakdown of the Born approximation for larger or high-contrast anomalies, causing model mismatch and wrong singular-vector structure; strong mutual coupling among closely spaced antennas alters incident-field assumptions and invalidates analytic decomposition; inability to fully cancel artifact terms when M or N is too small or when antenna geometry cannot satisfy the symmetry conditions; sensitivity to calibration errors and unknown background permittivity/conductivity leading to biased S-parameters; measurement noise and limited SNR reducing singular-value separation and degrading subspace estimation; non-uniqueness or spurious peaks in highly cluttered or multi-anomaly scenes, especially when anomalies have low contrast; limited generalization from thin/point-like anomalies to extended or crack-like objects; requirement for precise knowledge or simulation of incident fields for vector construction; computational cost for high-resolution parameter sweeps and for experimental repeated trials; hardware constraints in practice (fixed antenna sites, no switching) may prevent realization of the theoretically optimal arrangements.
